## Reuse the boundary

The page source embeds any registered same-origin route with one directive:

```{.markdown shortcodes=false}
{{< bonito route="/widgets/control-panel" title="Cable controls" height="34rem" >}}
```

Widget implementations live in `src/widgets.jl`. Keep domain-specific controls in their own Julia files, return a Bonito `App`, and register only their route in the publisher.

For reusable toolbars, bind stable action names to the module that owns their meaning:

```julia
module PlotTools
function handle_toolbar(state, event)
    state[] = "$(event.namespace).$(event.action)"
end
end

binding = ToolbarBinding(PlotTools, session_state; namespace=:impedance_plot)

tools = toolbar(
    [
        ToolbarButton(:reset_view; icon=:reset, tooltip="Reset view"),
        ToolbarButton(:fit_view; icon=:fit, label="Fit view"),
        ToolbarDropdown(
            :display_layer,
            [:nominal => "Nominal", :envelope => "Envelope"];
            icon=:layers,
            label="Layer"
        ),
    ];
    binding,
    orientation=:horizontal,
    size=:medium
)
```

The callback receives a `ToolbarEvent(namespace, action, value)`. Names use lowercase `snake_case`; the constructor rejects duplicate actions and invalid identifiers before the page is served.
